sources.entry: pathlib - (Python standard library) A cross-platform, object-oriented path library.

summary.name: pathlib
summary.one_liner: pathlib is Python's standard library module for object-oriented filesystem paths, with pure path classes for string-only manipulation and concrete Path classes that also perform filesystem I/O.
use_cases: Manipulating Windows paths on a Unix machine or vice versa
Listing subdirectories and glob-matching source files
Joining and navigating filesystem paths in Python code
Changing file names, stems or suffixes
Converting between paths and file:// URIs
Expanding home directories and resolving symlinks
summary.what_it_does: ["Provides classes representing filesystem paths with semantics suited to different operating systems. Pure path classes (PurePath, PurePosixPath, PureWindowsPath) do string-only operations without touching the OS.", "Concrete Path, PosixPath and WindowsPath subclasses add system-call methods such as exists(), is_dir(), iterdir(), glob(), open() and resolve().", "Supports path navigation with the / operator, and properties such as parts, parent, name, stem, suffix and suffixes.", "Offers pattern matching with full_match() and match(), plus relative_to(), with_name(), with_stem() and with_suffix() for deriving new paths.", "Can create and parse 'file' URIs (RFC 8089) through as_uri() and Path.from_uri()."]
notable: Pure path classes can manipulate Windows paths on Unix and vice versa without touching the filesystem
Path.from_uri() and as_uri() convert between paths and file:// URIs
Part of the Python standard library, added in version 3.4
caveats: Instantiating WindowsPath on Unix (or PosixPath on Windows) raises an UnsupportedOperation error, so only the matching concrete flavour can be used
Calling as_uri() from PurePath rather than Path is deprecated and will be removed in version 3.19
Some concrete path methods can raise OSError if a system call fails, such as when a path does not exist
